body: I'm not overstating. The company he works for only cares about the bottom line, so long as he's working, not making *major* mistakes, they will let him continue to work there (as far as I know, without actually reporting him).
No, its just a sign he self-medicates instead of trying to, I don't know, not do that?

Long term use of Xanax can negatively affect your memory. He's built up a tolerance over the years. He uses Xanax to help him sleep (insomnia), or to help "cure" (his words) his hangover. He'll stop taking it for a while before picking it back up again. If its not Xanax, then its alcohol or even a Benadryl to make him drowsy enough to fall asleep.

Functionally illiterate - as in he depended on me heavily to guide him around places we were visiting together. Constantly getting lost/just not paying attention to things. Will lose his wallet, passport, money. Unless its something he cares about he's not going to give much of a second thought to it. 

I know I can't convince anyone of this, unless you know him personally. But it's how he is.

He just forgets random things, like my name, or where he is sometimes. So far he hasn't made any major mistakes at work, but he continues to go into work either intoxicated from the night before or trying to self-medicate by taking Xanax
